# Mark directions

Two rounds were drawn as single ink vectors on a 64 unit square and rendered at 16, 32 and 256 px on the site ground in bone, on the app ground in lime, and inverted on white. None uses a chat bubble, a sparkle, a robot, a brain, a network graph or a generic AI glyph.

## The mark: the jar

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="96" height="96" alt="The jar">

What it says: a vivarium as anyone keeps one. Glass around wavy strata, a sprout growing inside, a door at the base. A small contained world in layers, something alive in it, and a gate at its edge.

Why it fits: it carries the name and the product's warmth in one picture a stranger can name. It rhymes with the page's file object (an icon over hairlines, one recorded line) and with the receipt ledger's strata of keys and values. It is quiet enough for the site and specific enough for a taskbar.

Where it fails: it is an outline with interior detail, so it softens below 32 px. At 16 px it is a jar with a dot in it, which still reads as a jar. It never fills a tile the way a solid mark would, so inside the app icon it sits on a dark tile. The door in the base of a jar is a small stretch of the metaphor and it stays because the gate is the product's claim.

## The family

Jeff asked for the variety, not one icon, so the family ships beside the mark. Same language: wavy strata, glass, a sprout, a gate. Use them as section objects, empty states and illustration. Never as a second logo, never in a lockup.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="72" height="72" alt="Dome of strata with a sprout"> <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="72" height="72" alt="Cloche over wavy strata"> <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="72" height="72" alt="Strata V with a sprout"> <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="72" height="72" alt="Wave globe"> <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="72" height="72" alt="Seed world"> <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," width="72" height="72" alt="Cloche vivarium">

- Dome of strata with a sprout: a hill of layers with life on top and a door. The rooms section.
- Cloche over wavy strata: the most literal terrarium. The memory section.
- Strata V with a sprout: the initial, the layers, life rising from the valley. The engine section, the four commands.
- Wave globe: a round world of layers with a door. The one that survives 16 px best, so the favicon can be this if the jar ever fails in a tab.
- Seed world: the globe with a sprout. Reads as a fruit at small sizes. Large only.
- Cloche vivarium: the first round's glass over flat strata, a sprout and a plate. Kept for the illustration language.

## Retired

- The ledger tile. A rounded tile with three lines and a door. Jeff called it ugly and it is: a notes app glyph with a notch. Removed.
- The old dome, traced. The wavy PNG as one flat path. A beehive in one ink. Removed.
- The small cut of the cloche. A dome with a bar under it, weird at every size. Removed. The jar has no small cut.
- The strata V without the sprout is superseded by the version with one.

## The asset brief's open decisions, answered here

1. Tagline: "It knows you. Because you wrote it down." It is the page's headline, it is the product's claim, and it says what Vivary does rather than what you keep. "Your projects. Your agents. Your machine." is three possessives in a row, a pattern many local first products use. Both are built so the choice can be seen.
2. Palette: keep the site's and the app's separate. The mark is single ink and takes the text color of whatever ground it sits on. Nothing new is invented to bridge them. The numbers are in the Color section.
3. Wordmark: Big Shoulders 800, optical size 40, tracking +1%, exactly the header brand word, exported as paths. The question is closed.
4. The dome: replaced by the jar. Its idea, a contained world in layers with a gate, is the whole family.
5. Company attribution: not decided here. It is Jeff's call and nothing in this system depends on it.
